How to return your early ballot in Pima County
 Voting early or by mail is popular in Pima County. About 85% of voters in the 2024 Presidential Election voted by mail or early in person. That figure approached 90% in the 2026 Primary Election .
 Voters who receive an early ballot have several options for returning it in time to be counted in the Nov. 3, 2026, General Election . A new ID-verified drop-off process is also available this year.
 All early ballots must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
 Here are the options:
 Return by mail 
 Voters can return their completed ballots through the U.S. Postal Service using the postage-paid return envelope. The Recorder’s Office recommends mailing ballots no later than Oct. 27 to allow sufficient time for delivery.
 Use a secure drop box 
 A voter drops off an early ballot outside the Recorder's downtown location at 240 N. Stone. 
 The Recorder’s Office maintains eight secure ballot drop boxes available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Ballots can be deposited until 7 p.m. Nov. 3.
 List of drop-box locations 
 Interactive map of drop-box locations 
 Drop off at an early voting site 
 Voters can return completed early ballots at early voting locations during operating hours. No identification is required for standard ballot drop-off. 
 List of early voting locations 
 Interactive map of early voting locations 
 Use the new ID-verified option at early voting sites 
 At an early voting site, ask staff to use the ID-verified option. Voters can present an approved form of identification along with their completed early ballot in its signed and sealed Ballot Affidavit Return Envelope. Staff will verify the voter's identity and stamp the envelope as "ID Verified." The process is designed to speed up ballot processing by eliminating the need for signature verification. The stamped envelopes will be placed in a secure ballot box for subsequent processing and tabulation. 
 Use the new ID-verified option at any of 126 Election Day Vote Centers 
 This sign will be displayed outside of Election Day Vote Centers on Nov. 3. The ID-verified process differs on Election Day.
 Bring your completed early ballot in its signed, dated and sealed affidavit envelope to any Vote Center by 7 p.m. on Election Day.
 Proceed to a designated table for ID-verified ballots.
 A poll worker will check your ID, verify your voter registration information and ask you to sign the electronic poll book.
 The poll worker will then stamp the ballot envelope as ID Verified, initial the stamp and will allow you to place it in a designated drop-off box.
 You will receive a printed receipt for the accepted ballot.
 The ID-verified option can only be used for your own ballot.
 Use standard drop-off at any Vote Center 
 Under the standard process, voters can go to any Vote Center to drop off their own ballots or those of eligible family members, household members, or individuals for whom they serve as caregivers. No ID is required; those ballots go through the signature verification process. 
 The Elections Department will have signs outside each Vote Center to explain the drop-off options.

 Interactive map of 126 Vote Centers 
 Additional information 
 Track the status of your early ballot to confirm it has been received and processed
 Request a ballot by mail by Oct. 23 if you are not on the Active early Voting List
 Visit www.pima.vote for a one-stop source of Pima County election information
